Allows this app to turn off the screen and lock the phone. It claims no other device admin policy.
This is the only permission that lets an app lock the screen. Nothing else is requested.
Alternative to Device Admin. This service does not read the screen; it only performs the system lock action when you tap the tile.
Pick \"Quick Lock\" under Installed apps. On a sideloaded build you may first need Settings ▸ Apps ▸ Quick Lock ▸ ⋮ ▸ Allow restricted settings.
Locks the screen from a Quick Settings tile. Works from any app, not just the home screen.

Device Admin is the smoother route on a sideloaded build. The accessibility service does the same job without Device Admin, but Android 13+ hides its toggle behind \"Allow restricted settings\" first.
Swipe down twice, tap the pencil (edit) button, then drag \"Lock\" up into your active tiles. On Android 13+ the button below asks the system to place it for you.
To uninstall, revoke Device Admin above first — Android blocks uninstalling an active device admin.
